summary: The Big Bad Wolf is a fictional wolf from cautionary tales. It appears in several of Grimms' Fairy Tales. It became a generic archetype of a menacing predator. Tales include "Little Red Riding Hood" and "The Three Little Pigs". 19th-century folklorists saw a solar myth in Red Riding Hood. In that reading, the wolf is night swallowing the sun. Ethologist Valerius Geist argued the fables reflected real wolf attacks. They warned people away from forests where wolves lived. Disney introduced its version in the 1933 short Three Little Pigs. The short introduced the song "Who's Afraid of the Big Bad Wolf?". Its success led to several sequels. In each, Practical Pig defeats the Wolf. Laurence Olivier said the Wolf was supposedly based on Jed Harris. From 1936 the Wolf appeared in Disney comics. The comics named him Zeke Midas Wolf. His son, Li'l Bad Wolf, wants to be good. Li'l Wolf is friends with the Three Little Pigs. His own series began in Comics and Stories in 1945. The Wolf also appears in Disney television series, including House of Mouse.
